City-level: A very tall, slender Gothic church spire rises on-axis ahead beyond a river bridge. A single, extremely high, lace-like spire viewed prominently from a road bridge is a distinctive sight of Ulm, where the Ulm Minster (the world’s tallest church spire) dominates the skyline and is clearly visible from bridges crossing the Danube between Neu-Ulm and Ulm. Other German cities with major spires (e.g., Cologne’s twin spires, Erfurt’s multiple spires, Freiburg’s single spire) either have different counts/shapes or typical vantage points not from a wide road bridge with this combination of modern lamps and low beige parapets. The silhouette and proportional height of the single spire best fit Ulm Minster. 
Street-level: The roadway appears to be a multi-use bridge with a right-side raised sidewalk and marked on-road bike lane, stone/beige parapet, and evenly spaced lantern-style lamps. Approaching the city center with Ulm Minster centered suggests one of the Danube crossings from Neu-Ulm to Ulm. The Herdbrücke provides a direct axial view toward the Minster with similar parapet color and lamp style, aligning with this perspective. Thus, the likely spot is the Herdbrücke, heading east/northeast toward Ulm Minster. 
Narrowing summary: Europe -> Germany based on signage, lane markings, and plates; Germany -> Ulm based on the single towering Gothic spire characteristic of Ulm Minster seen from a river bridge; Ulm -> Herdbrücke due to bridge details and centered alignment with the Minster.
